mainEntity.name: How is this different from pressure cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Completely. Pressure cleaning removes material by force. Soft washing applies a solution, lets it work, and rinses, so the growth is killed rather than knocked off and it stays away far longer.

They are not two strengths of the same thing, and on render the difference is permanent. Soft washing against pressure cleaning sets the two side by side.

mainEntity.name: Is soft washing strong enough to actually clean?

acceptedAnswer.text:
For biological growth it is considerably more effective than pressure, because it kills what is growing rather than removing the visible part. For heavy mechanical soiling on a hard slab, like ingrained traffic film on a driveway, it is not the right tool and we would use pressure cleaning instead.

Most properties need both, on different surfaces, on the same visit.

A biocide that kills mould, algae, moss and lichen, with a surfactant so it clings to a vertical surface long enough to work rather than running straight off. The exact mix changes with the substrate: a Colorbond roof, an acrylic render and a timber screen each need different chemistry and different strength.

It is diluted for the surface, not used at full strength because it is faster.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe for my garden?

acceptedAnswer.text:
With the standard precautions, yes. Beds are soaked before we start, which is what actually protects them, because a saturated plant takes very little up. They are rinsed again afterwards and run off is directed away from them and away from any pond or pool.

Tell us about anything unusual close to the wall when you book: a vegetable bed, a pond, an established fern, or a fish tank near an open window.

mainEntity.name: Why does the wall still look marked right after you finish?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Because some of it is still dying. Lichen in particular does not release the moment it is treated. It loses its grip over the following weeks and weathers off, and the wall keeps improving for a month after we leave.

That is normal and expected. If something is still obviously there after six weeks, tell us and we will come back.

mainEntity.name: Can soft washing be used on a roof?

acceptedAnswer.text:
It is the only sensible method for one. Pressure on a tile roof lifts and cracks tiles, drives water under the laps and can strip the surface off older concrete tiles. Soft washing treats the moss and lichen and lets it weather off over the following weeks.

The limiting factor on a roof is not the method, it is whether the roof is sound enough to walk on. Roof cleaning goes into that.

No, at these pressures there is nothing to damage it with. What soft washing does do is show you where paint is already failing: chalking, lifting at a join, or a patch that was touched up with a different batch. It did not cause that, it revealed it, and we will tell you before starting if we can see it.
